name: Mine Spoil-Heap Forests – Walk Rating & Choice Experiment
description:
Faithful replication of Braun Kohlová, Máca & Melichar (2021), "How High Is the Recreation Value of Successional Forests Growing Spontaneously on Coal Mine Spoil Heaps?", Forests 12:160. Part 1 (direct measure, 2 × 2 between-subjects): after viewing photos of the main forest types, each participant rates five forests in a random order: "How attractive would it be for you to walk one hour on the pathway in this forest?" (-2 not at all … 2 very attractive). Everyone rates the reference spruce forest (75 years), birch succession (55 years), alder and pine plantations (35 years), plus a randomly assigned 15- or 35-year-old successional forest; a label on the forest's origin is shown to a random half. Part 2 (discrete choice experiment): each participant is randomly assigned to one of four blocks and makes eight choices between two forest localities that differ in forest type, age and access time (5–25 min), or stays at home. The 32 choice tasks, their left/right layout and order were reconstructed exactly from the authors' published data (Supplementary Table S2). In the original study (869 Czech adults), all mine forests had a lower recreation value than the spruce forest, successional forests were not systematically less valuable than planted ones, recreation value grew with forest age, and the origin label had no effect.

Photographs: Braun Kohlová et al. (2021), Figure A1, CC BY 4.0. Used with credit for research; the template is removed if the authors object.

Differences from the original study: (1) each forest is shown with two photographs (as printed in Figure A1) instead of the original quartet of four; (2) English only (original Czech); (3) the five visual-feature ratings that followed the photo overview in Part 1 (reported in a separate paper, see template 2021-braun-postmining) are left out; (4) the wording of the "planted" forest-type label follows the paper's description, as only the spruce and succession labels are shown verbatim in Figure 3; (5) demographics are limited to gender, age and education, and a consent checkbox was added.

elements.description: Part 1, 2 x 2 between-subjects design (paper Table A1): every participant rates Spr75, Suc55, Ald35, Pin35 plus ONE of Suc15/Suc35 (random), in a random order; a label on the forest's origin is shown to a random half. Value: {attractiveness -2 not at all attractive .. 2 very attractive, position, label_shown, fifth_forest}. Trial key = forest id. Analysis in the paper: ordinal logit with forest dummies (reference Spr75), Order, Label, region and demographics.

elements.description: Part 2 DCE: each participant is randomly assigned to one of 4 blocks and answers its 8 choice tasks in the original order; each task shows two localities (access time 5/10/20/25 min, forest type label, age, photos) and an opt-out. The 32 tasks, their left/right positions and order were reconstructed from the authors' published data (Supplementary Table S2). Value: {choice: locality_1 | locality_2 | stay_home, chosen_forest, block, task}. Analysis in the paper: multinomial logit with species dummies, Mine, Age, Time, Left, region and demographics.
